reviews.author: Renee
reviews.text:
Hidden inside Sayushin History Park in Seoul, there is a perfect place to relax after a walk!

If you follow the quiet path that branches off from the park trail and climb the stone steps, you will come to a simple wooden pavilion. The best part about this place, which has tables and chairs, is the panoramic view of the subway tracks from Noryangjin to Yongsan. Watching trains come and go through the cityscape is a truly special experience.

Next to the pavilion is the Park History Museum, which displays interesting artifacts. However, please note the following:

⚠️Closed every Sunday and Monday

⚠️ Operating hours: 9:00 AM to 6:00 PM

Perched high above the park, this hidden retreat offers both historic ambience and city views. It's a great place to sit and relax after a long walk. We especially recommend visiting in the evening to see the beautiful sunset over the railroad tracks!

reviews.author: Joey Joo
reviews.text:
Han River Defense Line Noryangjin Battle Site

City Description: Noryangjin Battle Site, Han River Defense Line
Address: 12 Noryangjin-ro 17-gil, Dongjak-gu, Seoul
Subject: Korean War
Type: Information facility
Area: No information
Topic/Category: Korean War
Jurisdiction: Seoul Veterans Affairs Branch
Administrator: Seoul Veterans Affairs Office
Year of incident: 1950
Facility size: small
Facility construction date: No information
​

Contents

Immediately after the outbreak of the Korean War, the 7th Division of the ROK Army fought in the Noryangjin area, which connects the footbridge and railway bridge over the Han River, delaying the crossing of the Han River by the North Korean army occupying Seoul.
​

# Review # (Please note that this is a subjective review!)

The Noryangjin Battle Site of the Han River Defense Line was not a place I visited on my own, but a place I discovered by chance while visiting Sayuksin Park. The information board designated the Noryangjin Battle Site Memorial Facility along the Han River Defense Line, so I looked for it.

There was no information from the National Memorial Facility Information Service of the Ministry of Patriots and Veterans Affairs, which designates and manages memorial facilities, so I searched for information on the Internet.

The exact point of the Noryangjin Battle Site on the Han River Defense Line is at the southern end of the Han River Railroad Bridge and can be viewed from the place where the information board for the Noryangjin Battle Site on the Han River Defense Line is located.

In order to understand the Battle of Noryangjin on the Han River, the concept of the ‘Battle of the Han River Defense Line’ is necessary.

On June 25, the North Korean army launched an all-out attack along the 38th parallel, shocking the resting South Korean army. After the outbreak of the war, our army soldiers resisted by launching hand-to-hand assaults to block enemy tanks, but due to the North Korean Army's enormous armored power, the collapse of the command system due to inability to communicate, and misjudgments due to lack of information, Uijeongbu City fell at 2 o'clock on the 26th, the Changdong defense line collapsed at 13 o'clock on the 27th, and the last remaining 25th Regiment in Miari retreated at 6 o'clock on the 28th, and the capital was captured at 12 o'clock on the 28th. The center of Seoul fell into the hands of the enemy.

In the early morning of June 28, 1950, when the Conservation Cooperation Unit of the North Korean Army's 1st Corps crossed Miari Pass and entered Seoul, the Chief of Staff of the South Korean Army moved the Army Headquarters to Suwon, reorganized the Siheung District Combat Command, appointed Major General Kim Hong-il (金弘壹) as commander, and ordered this unit to block the North Korean Army's crossing of the Han River along the Han River Line.

In a situation where the Korean army was on the defensive, the Siheung district combat commander, who took on important responsibility, gathered the troops withdrawing in disorder from the front lines, reorganized the unit, and integrated other units from the Gyeongin district into it and began building the Han River defense line.

At this time, the units that withdrew from the front not only lost most of their combat equipment but also withdrew without maintaining their organization, so these units were integrated and reorganized into the Mixed Capital Division and the Mixed 7th Division and deployed to the front of the Yeongdeungpo, Noryangjin, and Heukseok-dong areas, while units in the Gimpo area were deployed in the Gimpo area to prepare for the North Korean army's crossing operation.

Thus, the North Korean 3rd and 4th divisions, which had begun crossing the Han River on the night of June 29, were stopped in the Dongjak-dong, Noryangjin-Yeouido Airfield area until July 2nd. In particular, the South Korean Army's 18th Regiment, deployed at Yeouido Airfield, held its position until July 3, when friendly forces withdrew, and prevented the North Korean army from crossing the river, earning a distinction.

However, the communist army repaired the half-broken Han River railway bridge, allowed tanks to cross, and then put pressure on the Yeongdeungpo and Gimpo areas, forcing the Korean army to withdraw from the Han River defense line while engaging in local warfare starting on July 3.

In this battle, the South Korean army ultimately failed in its defensive operation, but succeeded in a delay for six days, gaining valuable time to collect scattered troops and lead to the participation of U.S. ground forces. On the other hand, the North Korean army lost the time to deliver a decisive blow to the South Korean army and suffered an operational setback (see Wikipedia).

The memorial facilities related to the Han River Defense Line Battle Site are as follows. (I haven't been there yet, but I plan to review after my visit)

​
Commander MacArthur Han River Defense Line Inspection Site - Yeongdeungpo Park, 275 Singil-ro, Yeongdeungpo-gu, Seoul (Yeongdeungpo-dong)

Monument to those killed in the Battle of the Han River Defense Line - Bondong Citizen's Park, 247 Noryangjin-ro, Dongjak-gu, Seoul

Monument to the Battle of the Han River Defense Line - Moved from Yanghwa Artificial Falls to Yeouido Hangang Park

Han River Defense Line Heukseok-dong Battle Site - 55 Hyeonchung-ro, Dongjak-gu, Seoul

Student Volunteer Army Memorial Monument - 172-12 Heukseok-dong, Dongjak-gu, Seoul

Yeonhui Hill 104 Battle Site - San 100-1, Yeonhui-dong, Seodaemun-gu, Seoul

Also, the Noryangjin battle site along the Han River defense line seems to be a hidden spot to watch the fireworks festival. Since it is inside Sayukshin Park, I have not been able to confirm whether it is possible to enter at night.

reviews.text:
We used the Anguk Building parking lot for parking, and were provided with a free parking coupon for one hour. It was about a 3-minute walk to the store.

​I ordered seasoned beef ribs, cheese steamed egg custard, and bibim naengmyeon, and the meat with the charcoal flavor was soft and delicious. The cheese braised egg custard was soft and savory, making it the perfect side, and the spicy flavor of the bibim naengmyeon went well with the meat.
The side dishes were good, and the store was spacious, so I was able to eat comfortably. It was easy to order using a tablet, and overall, I was satisfied with both the atmosphere and service.
